messages:
maria: Heads up — nightly evals flagged a weird class of failures for int4-quantized >=seq_len 2048. Failures are not crashes, the run just returns a truncated generation (partial sentence) and no error.

sam: ugh. which job? link?

maria: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/2026-03-10/quantize-eval/172345 — you can see ~18% of runs for model redwood/alpaca-q4_0 cut mid-token. logs show no exception, just early EOF from harness collector.

kai: can you paste a minimal log excerpt?

maria: sure

```
INFO  | eval.run: starting generation id=gen-482
DEBUG | runtime.streamer: sending chunk size=128
... (many chunks)
DEBUG | runtime.streamer: sending final chunk size=6
INFO  | eval.run: generator closed (socket EOF)
```

sam: interesting that streamer thinks it sent final chunk then socket EOF. that implies receiver closed early. which process owns the recv side in the harness?

maria: harness spawns a collector thread per worker that reads from the model runtime via a unix socket. suspect the collector might be dropping data under high memory pressure or hit a socket buffer limit.

kai: Could this be related to the new non-blocking collector change from last week? I remember a patch that moved to select + recv with MSG_DONTWAIT.

maria: yeah that's the PR: f3a9d2e — it used non-blocking recv and then sleep backoff. It passed unit tests but maybe an edge with long tails.

ops: I also saw OOM spikes on the quantized nightly nodes around the same runs — memory cgroup pressure causing kernel to kill the collector? dmesg shows LRU reclaim, not oom-kill.

sam: if it's not OOM kill, maybe the collector thread is starving: using small usleep backoff can let sampling loop progress faster than collector reads when seq_len large and many tokens queued, causing socket peer to hit write buffer high-water and then the model runtime to drop/close? Strange.

maria: I reproduced locally with the nightly container: `./tools/run_eval.sh --model redwood/alpaca-q4_0 --seq_len 3072 --batch 1 --seed 42` — after ~3 runs I get the truncated output.

kai: can you run with strace on the collector? `strace -f -e trace=network -p $COLLECTOR_PID` might show EAGAIN or short writes.

maria: did that, found repeated `recvfrom(... ) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)` then later the collector calls close() without logging an error. culprit is a missing check after the recv loop that stops on consecutive EAGAINs > N without distinguishing transient vs end-of-stream.

sam: so the non-blocking change assumes end-of-stream when recv returns EAGAIN for X cycles. With high seq_len and long tail token sizes we hit that threshold spuriously.

kai: fix proposal: revert to blocking recv with a deadline (poll with poll/epoll timeout) or keep non-blocking but extend the threshold and check for peer shutdown via getsockopt(SO_ERROR) / recv returning 0.

maria: quick patch I tested locally: increase EAGAIN threshold from 5 -> 200 and add explicit check for recv == 0 (EOF). That dropped failures to <1% in my run.

ops: can you open a hotfix PR and roll to nightly dedicated pool? We should also add a test that simulates long seq streaming with artificial EAGAINs.

sam: agree. Also add a small metric: consecutive_eagain_count per collector so we can alert if it spikes.

maria: filing PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4827 — includes test and metric. tagging @kai for review.

ci-bot: build queued for patch f3a9d2e-hotfix

kai: reviewing tonight, will prioritize. thanks for the triage and repro steps — that was fast :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team. I'll monitor next nightly once patched and report back here.
